items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: Dale did most of the work for four years... The job I did was wonderful... approached me about putting out a magazine.

ctx.x: Whose idea was it for the title, Jazz Record?

Probably not mine, because I'm not sure I would think of that. It was more like a newspaperman that would think of that than a musician. But Dale did most of the work for four years, until he finally gave it up. I'm talking about addressing envelopes, about bringing it to the printer, about reading type. The job I did was wonderful. I walked around like an editor, and I interviewed guys. I got them down in that basement, and we miraculously were always able to come up with a jug which now I think Dale always paid…

And they would relax in front of me, because it's easy to relax in front of somebody in your own trade. It's easy for me to relax now, because I'm talking in front of someone who's a musician. And so that was the policy. And it worked out very well. And it didn't harm me. We got so popular, between the -- not that the magazine was selling so great, because of the radio. Because pretty soon I lost that radio show, anyway.
